subject: Dedicated capacity — cluster sizing guardrails & phased ramp plan for Sequoia Health AI
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>
To: Dawn Park <dawn@sequoiahealth.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, 20 Apr 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Dedicated capacity — cluster sizing guardrails & phased ramp plan for Sequoia Health AI

Hi Dawn,

Thanks again for the deep dive yesterday. Attached is a concise proposal and a compact cluster-config CSV that lays out three distinct activation lanes we think map to Sequoia's short and medium-term needs. High level: we built the options to give you firm "guardrails" for predictable unit economics while leaving room for burst and regional fallback.

Summary of options (attached PDF has cost anchors + timelines):

- Option A — Lean baseline (Activation Lane: "Starter")
  - Dedicated minimum: 8 x A100-class GPUs (shared across east/us region)
  - Warm-standby burst: +4 GPUs on demand for short windows
  - Ramp: 0–30 days to activate baseline; burst available immediately
  - Use-case: low-volume inference + small-model bursty workloads

- Option B — Balanced steady-state (Activation Lane: "Standard")
  - Dedicated minimum: 24 x A100-class GPUs
  - Autoscale headroom: soft cap to 40 GPUs with prioritized burst policy
  - Ramp: 2-week phasing: 8 → 16 → 24 over 14 days; full SLA at day 21
  - Use-case: predictable production traffic with <220ms p95 target

- Option C — Throughput-first (Activation Lane: "Scale")
  - Dedicated minimum: 64 x A100-class GPUs (or equivalent quantized variants)
  - Phased activation over 8 weeks with monthly commit discounts
  - Use-case: aggressive throughput, model ensembles, large-batch reranking

Operational notes and guardrails:
- Minimum-guarantee lanes are priced to reflect reserved capacity and include a measured burst policy so you can keep user-facing latency stable during spikes.
- We recommend Option B as the pragmatic start for the first-year production rollout and Option A only for tightly scoped pilots.
- We can support mixed architectures (some quantized replicas + full-precision for SLO-critical endpoints).

Next steps we propose:
1) Confirm which activation lane you prefer (A/B/C).
2) Share a short traffic sketch (avg rps, peak rps, typical seq len) so we can finalize kernel/quantization recommendations.
3) Target kick-off slot: week of May 6 — phase 1 (baseline activation) with a coordinated test window.

I've attached: proposal_sequoia_20280420.pdf and cluster_config_lane_table.csv.

Happy to jump on a 30-minute ops call with your infra/procurement folks to align on timelines and contract terms.

-Jordan

Jordan Blake
Senior Solutions — Redwood Inference
jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com | +1 (415) 555-0192

--
Attachment stubs:
- proposal_sequoia_20280420.pdf (PDF, 2 pages: options & pricing anchors)
- cluster_config_lane_table.csv (CSV, lane-by-lane GPU counts & phasing)

From: Dawn Park <dawn@sequoiahealth.ai>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, 20 Apr 2028 12:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity — cluster sizing guardrails & phased ramp plan for Sequoia Health AI

Thanks Jordan — useful framing. A couple quick clarifying questions before we loop in procurement: 

- For Option B (24 GPUs baseline), what are the expected p95 latency and sustained throughput at 8, 16 and 24 GPUs for our current small model (seq len ~128, batch size ~1)? We want concrete anchors to share with our SREs.
- Can the burst headroom be configured as spot/preemptible capacity (for cost savings) and if so what is the expected cold-warm ramp penalty?
- Procurement note: our legal & procurement timeline is ~6–8 weeks. We'd like to avoid a large upfront committed spend if we can phase billing or convert a portion to a reserved+consumption mix.

Also please include SOC 2 evidence and any relevant audit logs retention options in the proposal; procurement will ask.

Best,
Dawn
VP Product, Sequoia Health AI

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sat, 21 Apr 2028 07:30:00 -0700
Subject: Internal: pricing anchors + recommended approach for Sequoia (note for Jordan)

Jordan / Aditya — quick internal note to land our ask before we send the follow-up: 

- Pricing anchors: recommend we present Option B as our default with two payment profiles: (1) Reserved monthly commit (12-month) with a 15% discount vs month-to-month, and (2) Hybrid: 6-month partial commit (baseline 18 GPUs) + metered burst beyond that. 
- For procurement flexibility: include an activation clutch that allows them to convert 4 GPUs of the committed block to on-demand within the first 90 days if traffic is lower than expected.
- Operational add: warm-standby of +4 GPUs in the preferred region to keep cold-starts <30s for KV cache builds; call this the "activation lane buffer".
- SRE anchors (rough): at 8 GPUs expect ~12–18 req/s sustained (small model); 16 GPUs ~28–34 req/s; 24 GPUs ~45–55 req/s. p95 latency estimates (with our tuned kernels, seq=128, batch=1): 8 GPUs p95 ~310–380ms; 16 GPUs p95 ~180–240ms; 24 GPUs p95 ~150–200ms. We should caveat those as model-dependent but useful for their SRE review.

Recommend we:
1) Send a short update to Dawn with those SRE anchors and a revised proposal that includes a hybrid billing option and SOC 2 link.
2) Offer a 2-week proof-of-concept on Option B with a reduced trial rate (credit) — helps compress procurement.

-L

Laura Bennett
Principal, Commercial Operations
laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>
To: Dawn Park <dawn@sequoiahealth.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwoodinference.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwoodinference.com>, procurement@sequoiahealth.ai
Date: Sat, 21 Apr 2028 11:00:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity — cluster sizing guardrails & phased ramp plan for Sequoia Health AI

Dawn — thanks for the quick follow up. Responding to your bullets and looping in procurement as requested. Quoted the core bits below and attached an updated PDF that adds the hybrid billing option + SOC 2 link.

> For Option B (24 GPUs baseline), what are the expected p95 latency and sustained throughput at 8, 16 and 24 GPUs for our current small model (seq len ~128, batch size ~1)?

See Laura's internal anchors (copied below). Short summary: 8 GPUs ~12–18 req/s (p95 ~310–380ms); 16 GPUs ~28–34 req/s (p95 ~180–240ms); 24 GPUs ~45–55 req/s (p95 ~150–200ms). We'll include an explicit test plan during the POC to validate against Sequoia's build.

> Can the burst headroom be configured as spot/preemptible capacity (for cost savings)?

Yes. Burst headroom can be configured to prefer spot/preemptible instances; however, this carries a cold-warm penalty. Our experience: when fall-back uses preemptible capacity without warm KV caches you should expect a temporary p95 degradation for ~30–90s while replicas rebuild caches. We model that in the SLO-calculator in the attached CSV.

> Procurement timeline & billing flex

We can offer the hybrid: 6-month partial commit (baseline 18 GPUs) + metered burst beyond the baseline. Also prepared a short trial credit (2 weeks) for Option B to help compress procurement. If helpful, we can phase billing monthly during the ramp window to avoid a large upfront charge.

Attachments: proposal_sequoia_20280420.pdf (updated with hybrid pricing) and cluster_config_lane_table.csv (contains the lane phasing & SLO anchors). Also: SOC 2 evidence link is included in the attached PDF and at https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-sequoia-proposal.

Suggested immediate next steps:
- Dawn: confirm Preferred Lane (A/B/C). Based on our conversation, we recommend you choose Option B.
- Proposed phase-1 start: May 6 — we'll provision baseline (8 GPUs) and then step to 16 on day 7, 24 on day 14 if metrics match the agreed acceptance criteria.
- I'll open a HubSpot deal record and send a draft DocuSign once you confirm lane & billing profile. HubSpot: https://app.hubspot.com/deal/23456

If it's helpful, propose a 30-minute meeting next Tue (4/24) 10am PT to finalize procurement questions.

Thanks — Jordan

Jordan / Laura — appreciate the detail and the hybrid option. Procurement is cc'd here.

We will proceed with Option B ("Standard") under the hybrid billing profile (6-month partial commit at 18 GPUs + metered burst). Please:
- Issue a provisional invoice for the 6-month hybrid commitment and send the draft DocuSign.
- Confirm acceptance criteria for the phase gates (day 7 and day 14) — we need the concrete metric thresholds (p95, error %).
- Procurement requests SOC 2 Type II report and an IP/processing addendum; I've attached our procurement intake address (procurement@sequoiahealth.ai) for any legal questions.

Technical anchors from our side: we need p95 <= 220ms (small model, seq 128) and baseline sustained throughput of 50 req/s. If you can commit to those in the POC acceptance criteria we can accelerate legal.

Let's take the 24 Apr 10am PT slot for the call and finalize.

Best,
